data.abstract: Transformer operation and maintenance is very important for the stable operation of the power system, at present, the staff has accumulated a large number of transformer operation and inspection reports, how to effectively use the above data to achieve the prediction and solution of transformer faults is the key to improve the efficiency of transformer operation and maintenance. This paper constructs a transformer intelligent fault diagnosis system that integrates knowledge graph and large language model. Through the fault text preprocessing, knowledge graph construction and the invocation of the large language model to build the transformer intelligent fault diagnosis system, and finally through the entity relationship extraction effect comparison and Q&A system subjective and objective performance evaluation, it is verified that the system can be targeted to solve the information correlation weakness and decision-making generation efficiency in the process of transformer operation and maintenance, and significantly improve the health management level of the transformer.

data.abstract: The development of multimodal large models and digital twin technology is set to revolutionise the methods of intelligent monitoring and maintenance for transformers. To address the issues of low intelligence level, single application mode, and poor human–machine collaboration in traditional transformer monitoring and maintenance methods, an intelligent monitoring and maintenance digital twin multimodal expert reasoning system, fine‐tuned on visual language‐based large models, is proposed. The paper explores the modes and methods for implementing intelligent monitoring and maintenance of transformers based on multimodal data, large models, and digital twin technology. A multimodal language large model (MLLM) framework for intelligent transformer maintenance, grounded on the Large Language and Vision Assistant model, has been designed. To enable large models to understand and reason about image annotation areas, an adaptive grid‐based positional information processor has been designed. To facilitate the compatibility and learning of large models with transformer Dissolved Gas Analysis data, a heterogeneous modality converter based on the Gram–Schmidt angular field has been developed. For the unified modelling and management of multimodal reasoning and comprehensive resource integration in human–machine dialogue, a central linker based on an identity resolution asset management shell has been designed. Subsequently, a visual‐language multimodal dataset for transformer monitoring and maintenance was constructed. Finally, by fine‐tuning parameters, a multimodal expert reasoning system for intelligent transformer monitoring and maintenance was developed. This system not only achieves real‐time monitoring of the transformer's operational status but also generates maintenance strategies intelligently based on operational conditions. The expert system possesses robust human–machine dialogue capabilities and reasoning generation abilities. This research provides a reference for the deep integration of MLLM and digital twin in industrial scenarios, particularly in the application modes of intelligent operation and maintenance for transformers.

data.abstract: Oil condition monitoring is a core component of the equipment condition-based maintenance system in power stations. Traditional threshold-based diagnosis methods can only identify post-event states and lack the ability to forecast oil quality deterioration trends in advance, failing to meet the preventive maintenance demands of power stations. To address this issue, this paper proposes an oil quality prediction and maintenance scheme recommendation framework integrating deep learning and large language models, and constructs a bottom-up Dual-branch Fivelayer Fusion Model (DFF). The model adopts TabNet to extract static oil quality features and temporal convolutional networks to capture long-term deterioration patterns, connects quantitative features with industry rules through the fusion layer, and completes domain knowledge adaptation based on the Qwen2-7B base model to generate standardized equipment maintenance schemes. Experimental verification was conducted using three years of on-site oil quality measurements from two power stations of a hydropower group. The results showed that the framework achieved an oil quality state prediction accuracy of 92.7%, reduced the missed alarm rate of abnormal risks to 4.3%, and reached an average early warning lead of 2.1 detection cycles. All indicators outperformed traditional threshold methods and single-model methods. This framework can effectively improve the accuracy and foresight of oil quality diagnosis, and provides a feasible technical path for intelligent operation and maintenance of power station equipment. Additional interpretability and generationquality verification further showed that TabNet attention weights, TCN fitting curves, rule-constrained prompt templates and postgeneration compliance checks can make the diagnostic path traceable from numerical indicators to maintenance actions. Scenario-level process tracing further showed that the representative transformer sequence achieved a mean absolute error of $\mathbf{1 . 0} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{L}-\mathbf{1}$ over twelve detection cycles, while the ruleverification stage intercepted premature shutdown advice and excessive re-inspection intervals before final scheme release.

data.abstract: Multi-source heterogeneous data processing for power transformers serves as a critical driver for the digital transformation of operation and maintenance (O&M). This paper systematically elaborates key technologies for full lifecycle data processing. Firstly, it defines the characteristics of multi-source heterogeneous data in power transformers. Subsequently, preprocessing methods are proposed, including text and audio data cleansing, as well as structured data normalization. Furthermore, an analytical framework is established that integrates structured data analysis and text mining techniques. The paper discusses data fusion technologies and demonstrates the effectiveness. Finally, future trends are prospected, highlighting the application of big data processing and large language models as pivotal research directions for advancing intelligent lifecycle management.

data.abstract: In the context of large-scale new power system access, the scale of the dispatch automation system is expanding, and it becomes extremely challenging for operation and maintenance workers to achieve efficient and accurate matching between fault descriptions and contingency plans in the face of a large amount of complicated data. In order to solve this problem and speed up the fault handling process, this paper proposes a fault profile matching algorithm for power automation systems based on a large language model and low-rank adaptive fine-tuning. The method reduces the consumption of memory and explicit memory for the training and prediction of the large language model by low-rank coding, and uses the language comprehension capability of the large language model to improve the accuracy and response speed of the automatic matching of fault phenomena and fault scenarios. Improving the understanding and recognition of keywords in the power domain by a large language model by freezing the weights of a large pretrained model and incorporating the power dispatch automation system fault profile information into the pre-training layer of the original Transformer architecture. This method significantly reduces the number of trainable parameters for the downstream task while retaining the text comprehension and querying capabilities of the original model, and demonstrates better performance advantages and accuracy for the field of fault profile matching in power dispatch automation.

data.abstract: As projects in the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) industry grow in complexity and scale, there is an urgent need for more effective information management and intelligent decision-making. This study investigates the potential of large language models (LLMs) to address these challenges by systematically reviewing their core technologies, application scenarios, and integration approaches in AECO. Using a literature-based review methodology, this paper examines how LLMs—built on Transformer architecture and powered by deep learning and natural language processing—can process complex unstructured data and support a wide range of tasks, including contract analysis, construction scheduling, risk assessment, and operations and maintenance. This study finds that while LLMs offer substantial promise for enhancing productivity and automation in AECO workflows, several obstacles remain, such as data quality issues, computational demands, limited adaptability, integration barriers, and ethical concerns. The paper concludes that future research should focus on improving model efficiency, enabling multimodal data fusion, and enhancing compatibility with existing industry tools to realize the full potential of LLMs and support the digital transformation of the AECO sector.
